title: Scope the customer question before collecting records
intro: For PCB suppliers serving semiconductor and electronics equipment, quality and operating teams need clear record scope, sources and review responsibility.

sections.heading: Define the customer question
paragraphs: Identify the lot, process step, time period and information requested. Use this scope to decide which records matter to the response.
Name who compares those records with the request, who resolves differences and who confirms the response.

sections.heading: Separate enterprise and production records
paragraphs: ERP supports enterprise orders, materials, planning and costs. Manufacturing execution solutions support production progress, lot records and quality information.
Identify the team or system maintaining each relevant source. Agree review responsibilities and unresolved gaps with factory teams before defining the solution scope.

sections.heading: Industry context: Wafer Works
paragraphs: Wafer Works / 合晶科技 in Taiwan / Shanghai produces silicon wafer materials through crystal growth, wafer processing and epitaxy.
The case connects silicon crystals to wafer-lot production history and provides visibility into progress, equipment status and epitaxy records with quality parameter limits.
This silicon-materials context helps quality teams discuss production record sources and scope. A PCB factory must define the records relevant to its own customer question.

sections.heading: Discuss your factory scope with the Vietnam team
paragraphs: Digiwin Vietnam assesses factory operations, advises on business processes and supports on-site solution transfer and factory acceptance.
Bring one customer lot question, the relevant record sources, a review owner and unresolved gaps to a discussion of your process and implementation scope.
